transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I thought I gave you a gift last time. I told you to go home, mourn him, let the memory fade, and yet here you are scratching at my door again.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I tried to do what you said.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If you had truly tried, you would be halfway to forgetting his face by now. The surface sun burns away ugly memories. Why did you turn around?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I got to the edge and just stopped.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stopped because you are foolish. I offered you a clean ending, a simple story to tell yourself: he was lost to the earth. Most of your kind would beg for that kind of mercy.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It wasn't simple for me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Everything is simple for humans: you live, you lose, you die. I handed you acceptance like a lantern in a storm. What, exactly, made you refuse it?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I realized I couldn't walk away.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you walked back into the mouth of a beast instead. That is not bravery, boy. That is a failure of imagination.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Maybe it is.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You agree too easily. It is tedious when you do not even defend your own stupidity. What did you think would be different this time?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn't think about that part.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You climbed down thousands of steps into the earth without a plan? Humans cling to plans like drowning men to driftwood. What filled your head if not a scheme to move me?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just the sound of my footsteps.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Footsteps are a rhythm, not a reason. Either you are hiding something, or you truly are this simple. Tell me what pulled you back from the rim when you were so close to freedom.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The silence up there was too loud.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Silence was the gift. Silence is the end of screaming. I offered you the conclusion of this tragedy—why did you reject the quiet?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It didn't feel like a gift.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you are ungrateful as well as foolish. Most would kill for the chance to walk away unharmed. What did you feel in that dust that was worse than this?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I felt like I was forgetting him already.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That was the point, little shadow. Forgetting is how the wound closes. Did you come back because you enjoy the pain?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No. I just couldn't let it close yet.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You speak of healing as if it were betrayal. You think suffering for him makes you a good brother. Do you think he cares about your suffering now?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know what he cares about anymore.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you are sacrificing yourself for a phantom. The deep eats memory first, then bone, and you are chasing something that may already be gone. Why persist when the bond has dissolved?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because he's still my brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You cling to that word like a drowning man to a stone. It drags you down, yet you refuse to let go. Why do you love the stone more than the air?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's the only thing I have left.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is a story you tell yourself to feel noble. You had the whole world left—the sun, the markets, the future. You threw it away to come back to a cave. Why?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: None of it mattered if I was alone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you are not brave. You are lonely. You fear the silence inside your own skull, so you came here to fill it with danger—did I name it correctly?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Maybe that's part of it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Pathetic, to see a creature with so much life act so helpless. I should close the gate and let you rot on the steps. Would you sit there and wait?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes, I would.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that with certainty. Strange. When you turned your back on the sky and started down again, what did you feel in your chest?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I felt like I could breathe again.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: To breathe in the dark requires lungs that reject the light. You are telling me the surface air choked you because it tasted of safety? That makes no sense to a survivor.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It didn't taste like safety. It tasted like running.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: And running is what prey does to live. You are prey, little boy, not a hunter. Why do you insist on acting against your nature?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't be safe if he isn't.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is a tether, not a thought. You are tied to him by a rope I cannot see, and it dragged you down these stairs again—against comfort, against sense. Is that what you mean?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. That's exactly what it feels like.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you are a prisoner of your own heart. I offered to cut the rope, to let you walk free and forget, but you found freedom unbearable. Why is the pain of the rope better than emptiness?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because the rope is real.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Real. The gold in my vault is cold and hard, but this stubbornness is warm. Stupid, but alive. You truly meant to sit on the steps until you starved?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I wouldn't have left again.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You have a terrible kind of patience. Not the patience of stone, but the patience of a wound that refuses to close. And I find I am... tired of sending you away.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't have anywhere else to go.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You speak as if the surface is a locked room and this pit is the only open door. Last time I thought you were merely frightened, but perhaps you are something else. You seem broken enough to belong here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not broken.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Whole things do not sink this deep, little boy. I told you to leave and live, yet you came back to damp stone and cold air. I rarely see such a determined waste of a heartbeat.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It isn't a waste to me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So certain, for someone trembling in his sandals. Perhaps the only cure for this particular insistence is to let the dark test it. I am curious how long your certainty lasts.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just let me look for him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You speak as if I am the only thing between you and him. The real barrier is your fragility. Still—I am bored of blocking your path.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So you'll let me in?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I am not granting you anything. I am simply ceasing to care whether you survive. You refused my mercy on the stairs, so now you may taste my father's hospitality.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't care what it tastes like.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then cross the threshold. You walked away from the sun twice to stand here, so take your prize—and the heavy silence that comes with it. The way is open.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm coming, Omar.
